scripts/aacr-miss-anatomy.mjs: The readback that turns one benchmark artifact into the table the next device is chosen from: it splits the goldens we commented near and the judge rejected by whether our comment at that site was itself accepted. It buys nothing and calls nothing, so it is not a check that can go red - it is the reading a person does after a run, and `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` now cites it instead of a hand count. Local tool: run it on the artifact you just downloaded.
scripts/extract-real-ground-truth.mjs: Rewrites the PR-review ground truth from public bug-fix commits, so running it inside a pull request would replace the dataset the pull request is being judged against. It needs the GitHub API and a judge model, and its output is committed deliberately. Local tool: run it when the dataset changes, not on every push.
scripts/measure-candidate.mjs: A developer's question — which tests name this file, and what do they say its coverage is — answered on demand for one path. It measures nothing on its own and borrows the run that is already happening, so a CI invocation would produce a figure about the file the workflow happened to be editing.
scripts/generate-comparison-report.ts: Runs the full CA-Bench industry comparison and writes docs/INDUSTRY_COMPARISON.md plus the dashboard. It is a document generator, not a check: wiring it today would either commit on every push or leave the document silently stale. Recorded in the roadmap as a generated-and-compared step, with the comparison and not the generation being the thing a gate can assert.
scripts/run-llm-bench.ts: A standalone DeepSeek review-quality benchmark needing DEEPSEEK_API_KEY. The same protocol is scored inside the repository by the evaluation protocol scorers and by the Martian harness, both of which run in workflows and publish artifacts; this entry point exists for a single run against a candidate model, which is a person's decision rather than a nightly job.
scripts/code-scanning-corpus.mjs: Walks the open code-scanning corpus and prints the per-rule and per-path tables a triage has to start from. It is a reader of somebody else's measurement: the alerts are produced by CodeQL and Scorecard, and the count moves whenever one of their scans finishes, so a workflow that gated on it would go red for a rescan rather than for a change. It also needs `security-events: read`, which is a permission surface this repository has been narrowing rather than widening, and iteration 117 already removed four scheduled jobs that re-derived numbers nobody read. Local tool: run it when security work starts, which is what `docs/SECURITY.md` tells the next reader to do.
scripts/aacr-merge-slices.mjs: Merges the artifacts of two dispatches over disjoint slices into the two artifacts the comparison job reads, so that a registration naming both halves of a corpus is answered on two hundred rows instead of a hundred. It buys nothing and calls nothing, and its inputs are the artifacts of runs a person has already paid for, so a workflow that gated on it would be gating on artifacts that may not exist yet. Local tool: run it after the second slice lands, then feed both outputs to `aacr-ablation-compare.mjs`.
scripts/anchor-rate.mjs: The readback that turns one paid artifact into the four numbers R-41 was registered against - the anchoring rate, precision among anchored comments and among the rest, and the 2x2 - so that §91's table can be rebuilt after the code that produced it was reverted. It buys nothing and calls nothing: its input is an artifact a dispatch already paid for, and a workflow that gated on it would be gating on a file that only exists after somebody spends money. Local tool: run it on the artifact you just downloaded, which is what `docs/EVAL-CONTRACT.md` §91 did.
scripts/polyglot-scale.ts: The scanner measured over three hundred real files, judged by the same third-party grammars the polyglot bench uses. **It is a local tool and not a gate** because its corpus is whatever this machine has installed - `node_modules` and a Python tree - so a CI run would measure a different sample and post a number nobody registered. It bought the three defects of §92: a backtick that blanked four standard-library files, an oracle that could not see a declared function, and a recall that could exceed its own precision because a name was counted twice.
scripts/witness-replay.mjs: Replays a paid review artifact against the file each finding stands in, so the index's structural facts and cross-file facts (is the line inside a declaration, is the declaration one this diff touched, does the comment name a declared callee) can be scored as selectors without a model. It reads a committed artifact and the GitHub API, writes a new artifact and buys nothing, so it cannot go red - it is the reading a person does after a run. Local tool: run it on the artifact you just downloaded; its output is committed deliberately.
scripts/cross-file-report.mjs: Measures the cross-file index in `packages/intelligence/src/review/index/repo-index.ts` over this repository's own sources: how many relative imports resolve, how many names cross a file boundary, and whether `ts.resolveModuleName` agrees with every one of them. It reads local files, writes `benchmarks/cross-file-index.json` with `--json`, and makes no network call and no model call, so it cannot go red - it is the reading a person does when the resolver changes. Local tool: run it after editing the resolver and commit the artifact deliberately; the test that guards the resolver is `packages/intelligence/src/review/index/__tests__/a-change-crosses-files-and-the-index-has-to-say-where.test.ts`.
